extracted.intended_audience: licensees, other persons subject to NRC jurisdiction, attorneys, and participants in NRC adjudicatory proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural requirements for filing, service, hearings, demands for information, civil penalties, and other processes in NRC adjudicatory proceedings under 10 CFR Part 2. Covers electronic filing, document form, timing, burdens, and related procedural standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Live testimony procedures and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: The presiding officer shall conduct any live testimony pursuant to its powers in § 2.319 of this part, except that no subpoenas, discovery, or referred rulings or certified questions to the Commission shall be permitted for this purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staff may present its response through live testimony rather than a written response if the presiding officer orders live testimony. The presiding officer's order denying a motion for live testimony is referenced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to delay hearing on immediately effective order
rubrics_metrics.description: The presiding officer may, on motion by the staff or any other party to the proceeding, where good cause exists, delay the hearing on the immediately effective order at any time for such periods as are consistent with the due process rights of the licensee or other person and other affected parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delay is discretionary and constrained by due process rights of licensees and affected parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of going forward on immediate effectiveness challenges
rubrics_metrics.description: The licensee or other person challenging the immediate effectiveness of an order bears the burden of going forward with evidence that the immediately effective order is not based on adequate evidence, but on mere suspicion, unfounded allegations, or error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the initial evidentiary burden on challengers to show insufficiency of evidence supporting immediate effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of persuasion for immediate effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: The NRC staff bears the burden of persuading the presiding officer that adequate evidence supports the grounds for the immediately effective order and immediate effectiveness is warranted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even though challenger bears burden of going forward, the staff retains ultimate burden to persuade the presiding officer of adequacy of evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expeditious decision and non-stay of immediate effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: The presiding officer shall issue a decision on the motion to set aside the immediate effectiveness of the order expeditiously. During the pendency of the motion to set aside the immediate effectiveness of the order or at any other time, the presiding officer may not stay the immediate effectiveness of the order, either on its own motion, or upon motion of the licensee or other person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presiding officer must act quickly but does not have authority to stay immediate effectiveness while the motion is pending.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of upholding or setting aside immediate effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: The presiding officer shall uphold the immediate effectiveness of the order if it finds that there is adequate evidence to support immediate effectiveness. An order upholding immediate effectiveness will constitute the final agency action on immediate effectiveness. The presiding officer will promptly refer an order setting aside immediate effectiveness to the Commission and such order setting aside immediate effectiveness will not be effective pending further order of the Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Orders upholding immediate effectiveness are final for that issue; orders setting aside immediate effectiveness are referred and are not effective until Commission acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consent in answer as waiver and binding order
rubrics_metrics.description: An answer may consent to the entry of an order in substantially the form proposed in the order with respect to all or some of the actions proposed in the order. The consent ... shall constitute a waiver by the licensee or other person of a hearing, findings of fact and conclusions of law, and of all right to seek Commission and judicial review or to contest the validity of the order in any forum as to those matters which have been consented to or agreed to or on which a hearing has not been requested. An order that has been consented to shall have the same force and effect as an order made after hearing by a presiding officer or the Commission, and shall be effective as provided in the order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consenting in an answer is effectively a relinquishment of rights to challenge or seek review on consented matters; consented orders carry full force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with backfit/modification requirements (cross-references)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the order involves the modification of a part 50 or a part 53 license and is a backfit, the requirements of § 50.109 or § 53.1590 of this chapter, as applicable, shall be followed, unless the licensee has consented to the action required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Several specific cross-references apply (e.g., §52.98, §53.1443, §52.39, §53.1188, §52.63, §53.1263, §52.145, §53.1221, §52.171, §53.1288) depending on the type of license/permit/design; these requirements must be followed unless the relevant party has consented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demand for information: contents and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may issue to a licensee or other person subject to the jurisdiction of the Commission a demand for information for the purpose of determining whether an order under § 2.202 should be issued, or whether other action should be taken, which demand will: (1) Allege the violations ... or the potentially hazardous conditions ... ; and (2) Provide that the licensee must, or the other person may, file a written answer to the demand for information under oath or affirmation within twenty (20) days of its date, or such other time as may be specified in the demand for information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demand must state allegations and specify the timeframe (20 days unless otherwise specified) for a sworn answer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Answer requirements to a demand for information
rubrics_metrics.description: A licensee to whom the Commission has issued a demand for information under this section must respond to the demand by filing a written answer under oath or affirmation; any other person to whom the Commission has issued a demand for information may, in its discretion, respond ... The licensee's answer shall specifically admit or deny each allegation or charge made in the demand for information, and shall set forth the matters of fact and law on which the licensee relies. A person other than a licensee may answer as described above, or by setting forth its reasons why the demand should not have been issued and, if the requested information is not provided, the reasons why it is not provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Licensees are required to respond under oath and must address each allegation; others may choose to respond or explain refusal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission action following demand for information response or nonresponse
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon review of the answer filed pursuant to paragraph (a)(2) of this section, or if no answer is filed, the Commission may institute a proceeding pursuant to 10 CFR 2.202 to take such action as may be proper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission uses the answer (or lack thereof) to decide whether to institute further enforcement proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civil penalty notice content and pre-proceeding requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Before instituting any proceeding to impose a civil penalty under section 234 of the Act, the Executive Director for Operations or the Executive Director's designee ... shall serve a written notice of violation upon the person charged. The notice ... shall specify the date or dates, facts, and the nature of the alleged act or omission ... and must state the amount of each proposed penalty. The notice ... shall also advise the person charged that the civil penalty may be paid in the amount specified therein, or the proposed imposition of the civil penalty may be protested ... by a written answer ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice of violation must identify the legal/regulatory provision(s) alleged violated and the proposed penalty amount and must inform the recipient of payment or protest options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civil penalty answer and administrative process
rubrics_metrics.description: Within twenty (20) days of the date of a notice of violation or other time specified ... the person charged may either pay the penalty in the amount proposed or answer the notice of violation. The answer ... shall state any facts, explanations, and arguments, denying the charges of violation, or demonstrating any extenuating circumstances, error in the notice of violation, or other reason why the penalty should not be imposed and may request remission or mitigation of the penalty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to answer within the time specified can lead to issuance of an order imposing the penalty; if an answer is filed, the Executive Director for Operations will consider it and issue an order dismissing or imposing/mitigating/remitting the penalty; the person may request a hearing within 20 days of the order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compromise, referral for collection, and payment methods for civil penalties
rubrics_metrics.description: The Executive Director for Operations ... may compromise any civil penalty, subject to the provisions of § 2.203. If the civil penalty is not compromised, or is not remitted ... and payment is not made within ten (10) days following either the service of the order described ... or the expiration of the time for requesting a hearing ..., the Executive Director for Operations ... may refer the matter to the Attorney General for collection. Payments are to be made by electronic fund transfer using the electronic payment methods accepted at www.Pay.gov. Federal agencies may also make payments by Intra-Governmental Payment and Collection (IPAC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific payment channels (Pay.gov, IPAC) and referral to Attorney General for collection if not paid. Compromise authority exists subject to § 2.203.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civil penalty amount limitation and continuing violations
rubrics_metrics.description: A civil monetary penalty ... may not exceed $372,240 for each violation. If any violation is a continuing one, each day of such violation shall constitute a separate violation for the purposes of computing the applicable civil penalty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory/regulated cap on penalty per violation and separate counting for continuing violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests to institute proceedings: filing methods and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person may file a request to institute a proceeding pursuant to § 2.202 ... Requests must be addressed to the Executive Director for Operations and must be filed either by hand delivery ... by mail or telegram ... or by electronic submissions, for example, via facsimile, Electronic Information Exchange, e-mail, or CD-ROM. Electronic submissions must be made in a manner that enables the NRC to receive, read, authenticate, distribute, and archive the submission, and process and retrieve it a single page at a time. The request must specify the action requested and set forth the facts that constitute the basis for the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electronic submissions must meet NRC technical requirements for readability/authentication; contact info and guidance provided on NRC website and email.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director's handling and Commission review of requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Within a reasonable time after a request ... has been received, the Director ... shall either institute the requested proceeding in accordance with this subpart or shall advise the person ... that no proceeding will be instituted in whole or in part, with respect to the request, and the reasons for the decision. Director's decisions ... will be filed with the Office of the Secretary. Within twenty-five (25) days ... the Commission may on its own motion review that decision ... to determine if the Director has abused their discretion. No petition or other request for Commission review of a Director's decision under this section will be entertained by the Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director must give reasons if declining; Commission's review is internal/on its own motion, not by petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: E-Filing requirement for adjudicatory proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents filed in Commission adjudicatory proceedings subject to this part shall be electronically transmitted through the E-Filing system, unless the Commission or presiding officer grants an exemption permitting an alternative filing method or unless the filing falls within the scope of paragraph (h)(1) or (2) of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E-Filing is the default; exemptions are available under specified conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative filing methods allowed by order
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon an order from the Commission or presiding officer permitting alternative filing methods, or as otherwise set forth in Guidance for Electronic Submissions to the NRC, documents may be filed by: (1) First-class mail; (2) Courier, express mail, and expedited delivery services; or (3) Email: Hearing.Docket@nrc.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternative methods are available only by order; guidance referenced on NRC website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of service accompanying filings
rubrics_metrics.description: All documents offered for filing must be accompanied by a certificate of service stating the names and addresses of the persons served as well as the manner and date of service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certificates of service must reflect exact methods and recipients; specific content requirements vary by service method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing completion definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing is considered complete: (1) By electronic transmission when the filer performs the last act that it must perform to transmit a document, in its entirety, electronically; (2) By first-class mail as of the time of deposit in the mail; (3) By courier, express mail, or expedited delivery service upon depositing the document with the provider of the service; or (4) If a filing must be submitted by two or more methods ... the filing is complete when all methods of filing have been completed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When multiple methods required, completion requires completion of each method; see also good faith transmission requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good faith transmission requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: For filings by electronic transmission, the filer must make a good faith effort to successfully transmit the entire filing. Notwithstanding paragraph (d) of this section, a filing will not be considered complete if the filer knows or has reason to know that the entire filing has not been successfully transmitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filers cannot claim completion if they know transmission failed; must attempt to ensure full transmission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification and authentication credential requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The NRC provides identification and authentication services that permit participants ... to access the E-Filing system ... Any participant or participant representative that does not have an identification and authentication credential must request one from the NRC before that participant or representative intends to make its first electronic filing ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Credential application available on NRC website; required before first electronic filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic filing formatting requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise provided by order, all filings must be made in an electronic format (i.e., computer files) via the E-Filing system in a manner that enables the NRC to receive, read, authenticate, distribute, and archive the filing, and process and retrieve it a single page at a time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed guidance on acceptable electronic formats is available on NRC website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling electronic portions that cannot be transmitted
rubrics_metrics.description: If a filing contains electronic portions that may not be transmitted via the E-Filing system for reasons of security or electronic format ... the portions not containing those sections must be transmitted electronically via the E-Filing system. In addition, portable storage media containing the entire electronic filing must be physically delivered or mailed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When only parts cannot be transmitted, submit transmitted portions electronically and deliver portable storage media with full filing; no exemption required in these circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical object inclusion rule
rubrics_metrics.description: When an electronically formatted image or graphic of a physical object would not provide sufficient contextual value, the physical object may be physically delivered or mailed for inclusion in the adjudicatory record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physical evidence may be submitted physically when necessary; no prior exemption required for such submissions under specified paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemptions from electronic filing and formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon a finding of good cause, the Commission or presiding officer may grant: (1) an exemption from the electronic transmission requirements to a participant who is filing electronic documents (permitting email or physically delivered portable storage media) provided formatting requirements are met; or (2) an exemption from both the electronic formatting and electronic transmission requirements, permitting paper filing by specified methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A filer seeking an exemption must submit the exemption request with its first filing and show good cause; requests after the first filing are granted only if interests of fairness require.

rubrics_metrics.name: Docket maintenance by the Secretary
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary shall maintain a docket for each proceeding conducted under this part, commencing with either the initial notice of hearing, notice of proposed action, order, request for hearing or petition for leave to intervene, as appropriate. The Secretary shall maintain all files and records of proceedings, including transcripts and video recordings of testimony, exhibits, and all papers, correspondence, decisions and orders filed or issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All documents, records, and exhibits must be filed with the Secretary as described in §§ 2.302 and 2.304.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document caption and docket number requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each document filed in an adjudication to which a docket number has been assigned must contain a caption setting forth the docket number and the title of the proceeding and a description of the document (e.g., motion to quash subpoena).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Captions must clearly identify the docket and document purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper document physical and copy requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Paper documents must be stapled or bound on the left side; typewritten, printed, or otherwise reproduced in permanent form on good unglazed paper of standard letterhead size; signed in ink by the participant, its authorized representative, or an attorney having authority with respect to it; and filed with an original and two conforming copies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional format requirements appear in the section for signatures and margins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page format: margins and spacing
rubrics_metrics.description: Each page in a document must begin not less than one inch from the top, with side and bottom margins of not less than one inch. Text must be double-spaced, except that quotations may be single-spaced and indented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formatting requirements do not apply to original documents or admissible copies offered as exhibits, or to specifically prepared exhibits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature requirements (paper and electronic)
rubrics_metrics.description: The original of each document must be signed by the participant or its authorized representative, or by an attorney having authority with respect to it. The document must state the capacity of the person signing; his or her address, phone number, and e-mail address; and the date of signature. The signature ... is a representation that ... the statements made in it are true ... An electronic document must be signed using a participant's or a participant representative's identification and authentication credential. Additional signatures can be added ... by a typed-in designation that indicates the signer understands and acknowledges ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For electronic signatures, include a typed signature block: 'Signed (electronically) by' plus name, capacity, contact, and date. Additional individuals must include 'Executed in Accord with 10 CFR 2.304(d)' or equivalent. Paper documents must be signed in ink. Unsigned or fraudulently signed documents may be struck.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation for service on first filing
rubrics_metrics.description: The first document filed by any participant in a proceeding must designate the name and address of a person on whom service may be made. This document must also designate the e-mail address, if any, of the person on whom service may be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure service designee and contact info are provided on the initial filing to facilitate service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance for filing and nonconforming documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Any document that fails to conform to the requirements of this section may be refused acceptance for filing by the Secretary or the presiding officer and may be returned with an indication of the reason for nonacceptance. Any document that is not accepted for filing will not be entered on the Commission's docket.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nonconforming submissions risk not being entered on the docket and will be returned with reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-filed written testimony and exhibit electronic file rule
rubrics_metrics.description: In any instance in which a participant submits electronically ... written testimony or hearing exhibits in advance of a hearing, the written testimony of each individual witness or witness panel and each individual exhibit shall be submitted as an individual electronic file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each witness's testimony and each exhibit must be a separate electronic file to facilitate record handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission service method (how Commission serves participants)
rubrics_metrics.description: Except for subpoenas, the Commission shall serve all orders, decisions, notices, and other documents to all participants, by the same delivery method those participants use to file and accept service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission mirrors the participant's filing/service method when serving documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may be served
rubrics_metrics.description: Any document required to be served upon a participant shall be served upon that person or upon the representative designated by the participant or by law to receive service of documents. When a participant has appeared by attorney, service shall be made upon the attorney of record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serve the designated representative or attorney if participant is represented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method of service accompanying a filing (general rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Service must be made electronically to the E-Filing system. In accordance with § 2.302(g)(2) or (3) or upon an order ... service may be made by personal delivery, courier, expedited delivery service, or by first-class, express, certified or registered mail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default service is electronic; exceptions and orders may permit alternative service methods; participants not able to serve electronically should be served by the most expeditious available means unless undue burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service rules for participants with exemptions
rubrics_metrics.description: A participant granted an exemption under § 2.302(h)(1) will serve the presiding officer and the participants in the proceeding that filed electronically by email or by physically delivering or mailing portable storage media containing the electronic document. A participant granted an exemption under § 2.302(h)(2) will serve the presiding officer and the other participants in the proceeding by physically delivering or mailing a paper copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exemption type determines allowable service method; ensure certificate of service reflects actual methods used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of service content depending on methods used
rubrics_metrics.description: If a document is served on participants through only the E-filing system, then the certificate of service must state that the document has been filed through the E-Filing system. If a document is served on participants by only a method other than the E-Filing system, then the certificate of service must state the name, address, and method and date of service for all participants served. If a document is served on some participants through the E-Filing system and other participants by another method of service, then the certificate of service must include a list of participants served through the E-filing system, and it must state the name, address, and method and date of service for all participants served by the other method of service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certificates must detail exactly who was served by which methods and when.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of demonstrative evidence and non-filing service methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Service of demonstrative evidence, e.g., maps and other physical evidence, may be made by first-class mail in all cases, unless the presiding officer directs otherwise or the participant desires to serve by a faster method. In instances when service of a document ... will not accompany a filing with the agency, the participant may use any reasonable method of service to which the recipient agrees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrative evidence has specific permissive service method; parties may agree on reasonable alternatives for standalone service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service on the Secretary: methods and addresses
rubrics_metrics.description: All motions, briefs, pleadings, and other documents must be served on the Secretary of the Commission by the same or equivalent method ... Service of demonstrative evidence ... on the Secretary ... may be made by first-class mail ... The addresses for the Secretary are: (i) Internet: The E-Filing system at https://www.nrc.gov/site-help/e-submittals.html (ii) First-class mail: Office of the Secretary ... (iii) Courier ... (iv) Email: Hearing.Docket@nrc.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure service on the Secretary is contemporaneous with service on the presiding officer and participants; use the listed addresses/methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: When service is complete
rubrics_metrics.description: Service upon a participant is complete: (1) By the E-Filing system, when filing electronically to the E-Filing system is considered complete under § 2.302(d). (2) By personal delivery, upon handing the document to the person, or leaving it at his or her office with that person's clerk ... (3) By mail, upon deposit in the United States mail, properly stamped and addressed; (4) By expedited service, upon depositing the document with the provider of the expedited service; or (5) When service cannot be effected by a method provided ... by any other method authorized by law. (6) When two or more methods of service are required, service is considered complete when service by each method is complete under paragraphs (f)(1)-(4) of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Completion rules vary by method; when multiple methods are used, all applicable completions must be satisfied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service on NRC staff procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Service shall be made upon the NRC staff of all documents required to be filed with participants and the presiding officer in all proceedings ... Service upon the NRC staff shall be by the same or equivalent method as service upon the Office of the Secretary and the presiding officer ... If no attorney representing the NRC Staff has filed a notice of appearance ... service will be made using specified addresses ... If the NRC staff decides not to participate as a party ... it shall ... designate a person and address for service of documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow specified addresses when staff has not entered an appearance; staff must designate service address if not participating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation of time: general rule
rubrics_metrics.description: In computing any period of time, the day of the act, event, or default after which the designated period of time begins to run is not included. The last day of the period so computed is included unless it is a Saturday or Sunday, a Federal legal holiday at the place where the action or event is to occur, or a day upon which ... NRC Headquarters does not open for business, in which event the period runs until the end of the next day that is not a Saturday, Sunday, Federal legal holiday, or emergency closure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time computation is governed by the standard exclusion of the day of the triggering act and inclusion of the last day unless it falls on nonbusiness days at the place of action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation of time: added days for mail/express and mixed service
rubrics_metrics.description: If a notice or document is served upon a participant, by first-class mail only, three (3) calendar days will be added to the prescribed period for all the participants in the proceeding. If ... by express mail or other expedited service only, two (2) calendar days will be added ... If a document is to be served by multiple service methods ... the additional number of days is computed according to the service method used to deliver the entire document ... The presiding officer may determine the calculation ... in mixed service proceedings when all participants are not using the same filing and service method ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional days depend on service method(s); presiding officer has discretion in mixed-method cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness: specific daily deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: To be considered timely, a document must be served: (1) By 5 p.m. Eastern Time for a document served in person or by expedited service; and (2) By 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time for a document served by the E-Filing system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different deadlines apply depending on service method; use Eastern Time cutoffs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension and reduction of time limits; delegated authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as otherwise provided by law, the time fixed or the period of time prescribed for an act ... may be extended or shortened either by the Commission or the presiding officer for good cause, or by stipulation approved by the Commission or the presiding officer. If this part does not prescribe a time limit for an action to be taken in the proceeding, the Commission or the presiding officer may set a time limit for the action. The Secretary is delegated authority to issue orders establishing procedures and timelines for submitting and resolving requests for access to safeguards information or to sensitive unclassified non-safeguards information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions/reductions require good cause or approved stipulation; Secretary has delegated authority for timelines related to sensitive information access.
